title: URLs, Paths and Query Strings
learning_objectives: Split a URL into scheme, host, port, path, query and fragment
Decode percent-encoding and '+' in query strings
Represent repeated query parameters as lists
Compare a manual parser with urllib.parse
hints: `scheme, sep, rest = url.partition("://")`; then split off `#fragment`, then `?query`, then the first `/` separates host[:port] from the path.
Build a `bytearray`: for `%` append `int(text[i+1:i+3], 16)`, for `+` append a space, otherwise `out += ch.encode("utf-8")`; finally `out.decode("utf-8")`.
In `build_query`, encode each value with `.encode("utf-8")` and loop over the bytes: `chr(b) in SAFE_CHARS` → literal, `b == 32` → `+`, else `f"%{b:02X}"`.

failure_feedback.advice: Remove the fragment first, then the query, then split host and port at ':'.
Use port 80/443 when missing and '/' for an empty path; reject other schemes.
Collect raw bytes and decode them together with UTF-8; reject a lone '%'.
Skip empty pieces, keep every value of repeated keys in a list, and decode both sides.
Split each pair at the first '=' only.
Encode spaces as '+', unsafe bytes as upper-case %XX.
